info.title: Building58 relay
info.description: The relay passes commands to a world's page and runs the room: tickets, tasks, sessions and reviews. It answers this computer only. Each route's description is the manual's, from docs/manual/relay.html, where the fields, the tokens and the errors are.

servers.description: The relay on this computer. npm run office starts it on 8787.

{"text"}: a post, up to 500 characters. A session cannot post in #office, and posts at most once every 5 seconds in each ticket's chat channel and once a minute in each fun one. 409 archived in an archived chat channel, for the person too. Like the read, it makes an open ticket's missing chat channel first.

get.summary: List checkouts, or start a session in a new one.
get.description:
List checkouts, or start a session in a new one. A prompt can have up to 8000 characters, and a longer one is refused with bad_prompt. For a review of a PR, the relay then adds the reviewer's brief, and the verdict ask unless the body has auto. Those do not count toward the limit. A review of a PR can send unlessAt, the commit its last review read. While the PR is still at that commit, nobody starts and the answer says unchanged.

get.summary: What the Lead sees of the Floor, and each session's desk: ticket, title, column, pr, ciWords, review, doing, next (text
get.description:
What the Lead sees of the Floor, and each session's desk: ticket, title, column, pr, ciWords, review, doing, next (text and owner) and stop (safe and reason). The Lead's row also has tired, and every other row has null there. A Dev's row has waitsOn while the PR watch is on and its task has an open PR: owner, minutes, why, late and words. Every other row has null there. See What the Lead sees and What each desk says.

post.summary: With a session's token, {"who"}: the Lead stops one session.
post.description:
With a session's token, {"who"}: the Lead stops one session. Only the token of a Lead you let move the board, and only while Let the Lead stop sessions is on (or RELAY_LEAD_STOPS=1). See What the Lead stops. With the relay key, as the page sends it, {"who": terminal id} or {"all": true}: you stop one desk, or every desk, that its desk calls safe to stop at that moment. The Lead's desk is never safe to stop. GET /floor also gives leadEnded: null while a Lead runs or nothing is offered back, or, once the Lead's session ended in this run, how it ended (stopped, ended or crashed) and a sentence that says so. One that is not safe is refused with not_safe and the reason. See What each desk says.

post.summary: {"pr", "head", "text"}: marks a PR ready to merge.
post.description:
{"pr", "head", "text"}: marks a PR ready to merge. Only the Lead's token, or the relay key. The relay checks the PR with gh, posts one comment headed Ready to merge, adds the ready to merge label, and takes the label off when a new commit lands. A PR that fails a check gets 409 and not_ready, a note with a part missing gets 400, and a gh failure gets 502. See Ready to merge.

post.description:
Make a plain session the Lead (terminal), which saves it and gives it the Lead's brief. Answer the offer to bring it back (asked: true; POST /terminals with resume and lead: true is what Bring back sends). With board: true or false, give or take away its permission to move the board. With starts and total, give it permission to start tickets while fewer than starts tasks are building (1 to one under the WIP limit), total in all (1 to 20), or take it away (starts: 0). With refresh: true or false, start or stop Refresh the Lead. With "lead": true, as Settings sends, a grant goes only to the session that is the Lead now, and is refused with not_lead otherwise, so a page that has not seen another session made the Lead does not make the old one the Lead again.

get.summary: List or file tickets.
get.description:
List or file tickets. The list comes in Board order: open tickets high, normal, low, in work order (rank) within each, then done and rejected ones, the latest changed first. It also has kinds (the kinds a ticket can have, see Kind), labels (the labels tickets have, A to Z, see Labels), wipLimit, leadStarts (the number you let the Lead start tickets up to, or 0) and leadStartsLeft. A ticket has approvedBy (you or Lead) once it is put in Ready. The room page gets the same list as a tickets event on its GET /stream when it opens the stream with board=1, with people, who sits on each ticket, and without the time each pipeline was checked. The stream's hello says whether it will (tickets). It is sent once as the stream opens, then only when it changes, and only to the room page on this computer.

{"action", "ids", "why"}: proposes to change a Triage or Ready ticket. action is replace (with one or more ids), merge (with one), close (with none) or blockers (the whole new list, which can be empty). why is up to 500 characters. Nothing changes but the ticket's proposal, which holds it back. The PM's and the Lead's tokens propose, and so does the person's key, when the proposal then says You propose. Refused with 400 when an id is not on the Board, is the ticket itself, or was rejected, for every kind, and when a new blocker already waits for the ticket. A ticket that is starting, started, done or rejected gets 409, or 403 for a session's token. See Proposals.
